clue.text: Team has odd members leaving their bus

indicators.note: the letters in odd positions of the two words drop out, leaving the even-placed ones

explanation.surface: A team's awkward players are being thrown off the team coach.
explanation.walkthrough: HIBS is the nickname of Hibernian, an Edinburgh football club. Dropping the 1st, 3rd, 5th and 7th letters of 'their bus' leaves its even letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Familiar nickname of Hibernian, a Scottish football club, so a sports side.

clue.text: Criminal with horse: I may hang

definitions.text: Criminal with horse: I may hang

indicators.note: criminal signals the letters are crooked, set out of order

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for horse (as in horsepower's H)

explanation.surface: A mounted outlaw reflects that he may end on the gallows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' works twice in the &lit: as the anagram signal for W, H and I MAY HANG, and as what the whole clue describes.
explanation.definitionFit: A mounted robber of travellers on old roads was a criminal with a horse, often hanged.

clue.text: Flying starts for both yachts active in regatta

indicators.note: starts for points to the first letter of each following word

explanation.surface: Both yachts racing in a regatta make a flying start.
explanation.definitionFit: Travelling through the air is flying, as opposed to by sea or land.

clue.text: Smoother spin doctors prepare my English

indicators.note: spin and doctors both mean twisting or tampering with something, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Political spin doctors draft a statement in the speaker's own English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spin doctors' looks like the political advisers, but it is the anagram signal: PREPARE MY rearranges to MERYPAPER, after E.
explanation.definitionFit: Abrasive paper is used to smooth surfaces, so it is a smoother.

clue.text: Chart tune that for example breaks amplifier

indicators.note: breaks means splits open, so the example letters go within the chart

parts.note: a map is a chart
to hone is to tune up or refine

explanation.surface: A chart-topping song breaks through the speakers.
explanation.definitionFit: A cone-shaped device that makes the voice louder is a kind of amplifier.

clue.text: Approach series in buoyant mood

parts.note: a run is a series, as a run of wins
up means cheerful, in buoyant mood

explanation.surface: A winning streak puts someone in high spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: The period or path leading to an event is its approach.

clue.text: Excuse me: what comes before that in quiet message?

indicators.note: in places the musical note inside the quiet message

parts.note: p, piano, means quietly in music
a text is a message
in sol-fa, re is the note before me

explanation.surface: Someone apologises and asks what came before in a whispered message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that' points back to 'me', read as the sol-fa note mi: the note before it is RE.
explanation.definitionFit: A false reason given to hide the real one is an excuse.

clue.text: Punch worker, look, holding up ducks

indicators.note: holding means keeping inside, so the other pieces go within the look

parts.note: to peer is to look
taken as written
ducks and pet are both British terms of endearment

explanation.surface: A labourer gets a punch while looking at some ducks.
explanation.walkthrough: Punch is the puppet of Punch and Judy shows, so his worker operates him.
explanation.definitionFit: The person who works the Punch puppet in a Punch and Judy show operates it by hand.

clue.text: Fish to lift out of one's trap

indicators.note: trap is slang for mouth, so coming out of it means spoken

parts.note: to raise is to lift

explanation.surface: Someone tries to lift a fish out of a trap.
explanation.definitionFit: Rays are flat cartilaginous fish such as skates.

clue.text: Gift to press on girl

parts.note: a sop is a small gift to placate someone
to hie is to hasten, press on

explanation.surface: Someone is told to keep giving presents to a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Sophie is a common female first name, one instance of a girl.

clue.text: An alluring thing to play for a cricket team!

parts.note: glam is short for glamorous, alluring
an organ is an instrument, a thing one plays

explanation.surface: An exclamation praising a glamorous instrument as something to play for a team.
explanation.walkthrough: GLAMORGAN is the only Welsh side in English county cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Glamorgan County Cricket Club is a first-class side in the County Championship.

clue.text: Things in such a state after vacation

definitions.text: Things in such a state after vacation

parts.words: Things in such a state after vacation
parts.note: vacation here means vacating, leaving a place, not a holiday: once everyone has moved out, rooms are in this state

explanation.definitionFit: A vacated place has nothing in it, which is what this adjective describes.

clue.text: Do minimal money laundering when pinching Royal Navy asset

indicators.note: pinching means holding tightly inside, so the Royal letter is clasped within

parts.note: laundering clothes is doing the wash
1p, one penny, is the smallest sum of British money, written as I and P

explanation.surface: A crook does a little money laundering while stealing Royal Navy property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' just joins. 1p (one penny) is the least British money; R goes into WASHIP.
explanation.definitionFit: A fighting ship is a principal possession of any navy.

clue.text: Looked to have reached climax of speech

indicators.note: of speech means as spoken, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: to have peaked is to have reached the highest point

explanation.surface: Someone spoke of having hit a high point in a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: To peek is to glance quickly, so peeked is a past-tense synonym of looked.

clue.text: Set to obtain win, gave out

parts.note: to get is to obtain

indicators.note: out means disordered, so the letters of win and gave are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone ready to win gives up instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' turns WIN and GAVE into WEAVING.
explanation.definitionFit: The British idiom means start working briskly, much like setting to.

clue.text: One's acknowledgement to carrier on arrival: I'm stumped!

definitions.text: One's acknowledgement to carrier on arrival
definitions.meaning: what you might say to a driver or bearer who has delivered you somewhere
an admission that one cannot answer a question

explanation.surface: Someone thanks a taxi driver on arrival, then admits being baffled.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom admitting defeat over a question, and can also literally thank someone for transport.

clue.text: Knight visiting capitals entered without obstruction

indicators.note: visiting means calling in, so the knight goes inside the capitals

parts.note: uc stands for upper case, capital letters
N is the chess abbreviation for knight
logged means recorded or entered

explanation.surface: A knight touring capital cities has his entry recorded.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cleared of blockage is free of any obstruction.

clue.text: Ace crossing lake comes to medium whirlpool

indicators.note: crossing means going across, so the ace's word spans the lake letter

parts.note: a maestro is an ace, an expert

explanation.surface: An ace sailor crossing a lake runs into a whirlpool.
explanation.definitionFit: A maelstrom is a powerful whirlpool, originally one off Norway.

clue.text: Boy stores minute wild cress in water droplets: I'd drain mine!

indicators.note: stores means keeps inside, so the minute letter goes within the boy's name

parts.note: Archie is a boy's name

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters inside the dew

parts.note: dew is droplets of water

indicators.note: wild signals the letters of cress are scattered

explanation.surface: A boy keeps cress growing wild in dewy conditions, and boasts he could drain a mine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' turns CRESS into ESSCRE, which 'in' puts inside DEW. The device is an ancient screw-shaped pump, so 'I'd drain mine' is the machine speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: This ancient helical pump lifts water and was used for draining mines and fields.

clue.text: One disbelieving as diamonds drop close to batsman?

indicators.note: drop means falls lower, and in a down entry the letter moves further down

parts.note: an infidel is an unbeliever
D is the card abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: A sceptic watches as the diamonds fall.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the infield is the area close to the batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: The infield in cricket is the part of the ground near the wicket and batter.

clue.text: Hot meal goes in seconds: gracious!

indicators.note: goes in means the meal is placed inside the other letters

parts.note: my! and gracious! are both exclamations of surprise
tea is a meal

explanation.surface: A hot meal is gone in seconds, to someone's surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Steamy means hot and humid, or erotic.

clue.text: Prisoner cracking jaw

parts.note: con is short for convict, a prisoner
cracking and fab both mean excellent

explanation.surface: A prisoner breaks someone's jaw.
explanation.definitionFit: Jaw is slang for a long chat, as is a cosy talk.

clue.text: Spartan in ancient times touring most of continent

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the dates enclose the continent letters

parts.note: BC, before Christ, marks ancient times

indicators.note: most of drops the final letter

parts.note: Asia is a continent

explanation.surface: Spartans in ancient times tour much of a continent.
explanation.definitionFit: Spartan means plain and austere, a sense shared with this adjective.

clue.text: Opera set in hospital by a composer

indicators.note: set in means placed inside, so the opera house goes within the hospital

parts.note: san is short for sanatorium, a hospital
the Met is the Metropolitan Opera of New York

explanation.surface: An opera is staged in a hospital by a composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedřich Smetana was a nineteenth-century Czech composer, of The Bartered Bride.

clue.text: Head on arm, bottom in the air

indicators.note: head on means the first letter of arm

parts.note: the foot is the bottom of something

explanation.surface: A gymnast's head is on an arm with legs in the air.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in the air is happening or in preparation, the idiomatic sense here.

clue.text: Girl's last letter found on a drawer

parts.note: Z is the last letter of the alphabet
RA, Royal Academician, is an artist, one who draws

explanation.surface: A girl's final letter is found on top of a chest of drawers.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Zara is a female first name, so it names one particular girl.

clue.text: Fit cases for, ultimately, debate

indicators.note: cases means encloses, so the fit wraps around the letter

parts.note: an ague is a fit of shivering fever

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word for

explanation.surface: Someone builds suitable cases for a debate.
explanation.definitionFit: To argue is to dispute or put a case, a verb sense of debate.

clue.text: Italian hothead's instant comeback in Bristol ground

indicators.note: in puts the turned word inside the scrambled letters
ground means crushed and reduced, so Bristol's letters are broken up
comeback means the word for instant is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a mo is a moment, an instant

explanation.surface: An Italian with a temper makes a quick retort at a Bristol football ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' turns BRISTOL into STRBOLI; 'comeback' turns MO into OM, which goes 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Stromboli is a constantly erupting volcanic island off Sicily, a mountain with a fiery top.

clue.text: Assistant, vain at heart, gave up backing a politician

indicators.note: at heart takes the central letters of vain
backing means the word for gave up is read from the end

parts.note: ceded means gave up or surrendered
MP, Member of Parliament, is a politician

explanation.surface: A vain assistant abandoned support for a politician.
explanation.definitionFit: An officer acting as a senior commander's personal helper is an assistant.

clue.text: One who's been blessed with answer? Good for him!

definitions.text: One who's been blessed with answer? Good for him!

parts.note: St is short for saint, a holy person

explanation.surface: A man blessed with a positive answer is congratulated.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue suggests a groom-to-be who has been given a yes to his proposal, celebrated at his party.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridegroom's last fling before marriage is a male-only party, named after the male deer.
